content.title: How an Ousmane Dembele brace for PSG knocked Liverpool out of the Champions League to secure semi-final place
content.text: Reigning champions PSG secured their spot in the last four with a comfortable win over Liverpool across two legsOusmane Dembele celebrates his first goal for PSG at Anfield Getty ImagesLiverpool 0-2 PSG (0-4 agg.) — reactionPSG are through to the Champions League semi-final after beating Liverpool 2-0 in their quarter-final second leg at Anfield.With a two goal aggregate lead after the first leg, an Ousmane Dembele brace sealed the reigning champions’ place in the final four with a comprehensive 4-0 win on aggregate. Hugo Ekitike was forced off with a serious injury in the first half, while after the break Liverpool had a penalty decision overturned as they pushed for a goal. Liverpool will end their second season under manager Arne Slot without a trophy after their exit in the final eight.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comRead The Athletic's live schedule for the week hereSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementThe Briefing: Liverpool 0-2 PSG (0-4 agg.)Missed tonight's match?Want to know what made PSG tick and how they unpicked Liverpool so easily?Then look no further than The Briefing, where our writers tuck into all the big topics from the biggest matches. Dive in below.Luis Enrique: ‘We need to grow’PSG coach Luis Enrique has told Prime Video that his side need to be even better than last season if they want to win a second successive Champions League.💬 “It’s a different history because last year everybody felt we could not win the Champions League because we were so young.“Now, everybody knows we are the champions but we need to grow and I think we can grow.”Coming up tomorrow...There are two more Champions League quarter-final second legs to come with Real Madrid hosting Bayern Munich (covered live on The Athletic) and Arsenal hosting Sporting CP tomorrow.Those games both begin at 8pm BST in the UK, which is 3pm ET and 12pm PT in the U.S.PSG will face either Madrid or Bayern in the semis, while Atletico will meet Arsenal or Sporting CP. More from Konate Getty ImagesSpeaking to Prime Video, Ibrahima Konate laid down a challenge for Liverpool to get back in the Champions League for next season after their defeat against PSG.💬 “It's the minimum standard for Liverpool to be in the Champions League.“We have six games left and during these six games we have to give it our all.“We know how difficult the Premier League is but we have to give it all to be in the Champions League next season again.”Konate said Liverpool got less than they deserved in the second leg but admitted they got off lightly with a 2-0 defeat in last week’s first leg in Paris.💬 “When we played there they had many chances and only scored two.“At Anfield we could maybe do something special and today we created many chances and on the pitch we were probably the better team, that’s why it’s a little bit unfair.“We created so many chances to score and in the end they had maybe only one or two clear chances, but this is football.”Slot provides Ekitike updateThis is latest word on Hugo Ekitike’s injury, which looked to be a serious one. Here’s what his boss Arne Slot had to say:💬 “Not too good, we could all see that he did not look to well or too good. In the second half he went home so I haven’t seen him yet. “Losing the game is already very hard in the way we lost it. But then as it seems to be, losing a player is something we have had many times this season. It is especially hard for him because you never want to be injured, not at this moment of time in the season.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementKonate on Ekitike: ‘I send him my prayers’ Ibrahima Konate sent out a worrying message on team-mate Hugo Ekitike, who left the field on a stretcher before half-time.Speaking to Prime Video, the defender raised concerns about his team-mate’s chances of making the summer’s World Cup.💬 “We have to be happy, we had many players who came back from injury.“Ekitike, I’m very sad for him and I hope he will come back.“To be fair I think it’s bad. I heard many things. I have no words to talk about that. With the World Cup coming up this summer it’s very hard for him at this moment and I send him my prayers and everything.”Match dashboard: Liverpool 0-2 PSG Enjoy number crunching? Well take a look at the match dashboard for this one, which shows that Liverpool had a higher expected goals tally from that match than PSG.The only numbers that matters, though, are on the scoreboard and PSG were the winners there.Let's hear from Arne SlotThe Liverpool manager has been speaking to Prime Video as he reflected on his side exiting the Champions League. Here’s what he had to say:💬 “We got much more than we deserved last week by only losing 2-0. That was the same last season. What was the same as last season is that today we got less than we deserved. “Today, we should have won but it’s the quality of them that they did not concede from all the chances we had. “The finish from Demebele tells you why he won the Ballon D’Or, why they won the Champions League last season and why they have a good chance to win it again this season.”What next for Arne Slot? There is plenty of time for a summer rebuild and a full debrief for Arne Slot to digest what went right and what went wrong this season.But there is no denying that he is under some pressure, enduring a difficult campaign after the highs of his first year in charge.PSG fight on That was a classy performance from the holders, who showed just why they won the competition last season. Defending the Champions League title is a rare thing indeed — could they do it this year?SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWill Mohamed Salah add to his Champions League tally? So it's 47 Champions League goals and out for Mohamed Salah at Liverpool.He brought up 50 career goals in the competition in spectacular fashion against Galatasaray in the previous round, but ultimately will have wanted more in Europe this season. Whether he gets to add to that tally depends on where he will be playing club football next season. Salah's Liverpool career will end without another trophy After bringing so much success to Liverpool over the years, Mo Salah will bow out at the end of the season without any more silverware from this season.Liverpool have struggled as a team in transition from the old guard to something new — Salah will be sad not to have won one more trophy this year.A picture paints a thousand words If you wanted a photo to sum up the night, and probably Liverpool's season, then a sad Arne Slot in the rain probably does it. A difficult second campaign as Liverpool boss.Tough night for Mac Allister It never rains but it pours, and that was the case at Anfield for Alexis Mac Allister.First the midfielder won his side a penalty with a foul by Willian Pacho, only for VAR to intervene and convince the referee to overturn the decision.Then he was beaten too easily on the edge of the box by Ousmane Dembele for the opening PSG goal.Another great night for PSG against English opposition Getty ImagesOver the past two seasons, PSG have now knocked Liverpool (twice), Aston Villa, Arsenal and Chelsea out of the Champions League.They love playing against English teams right now. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDembele clinical for PSG Getty ImagesOusmane Dembele was not overly involved at times tonight.But he had six shots, got three on target and scored two goals from an xG of 1.05.He gave his side the clinical edge that Liverpool lacked.Ekitike injury looks troubling for him and LiverpoolIt was immediately clear that Hugo Ekitike’s night was over.There was no-one near Liverpool’s 17-goal top scorer when he went down in agony clutching his right leg shortly before the half-hour mark. The manner in which players from both sides rushed to comfort him underlined the severity of the situation.Ekitike has proved a big hit at Anfield since arriving from Eintracht Frankfurt in a £79million deal last summer.His absence will be keenly felt and it’s another body blow for Liverpool in a season packed full of injury setbacks.Atletico Madrid also through to the semi-finalsAtletico Madrid will join PSG in the final four of this year's Champions League.They lost to Spanish rivals Barcelona 2-1 tonight after Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres scored for the visitors, but Ademola Lookman got a crucial goal back for Atletico for a 3-2 aggregate victory.Barcelona had another Torres strike ruled out in the second half before Eric Garcia was sent off with 11 minutes remaining.Ngumoha a rare bright spot for Liverpool Getty ImagesIt's hard to find any positives from Liverpool's night. They were beaten 2-0, knocked out of Europe, and saw their striker go off with what looked like a worrying injury.But one glimmer of light was the introduction of 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha in the second half. He scored against Fulham at the weekend and looked lively once more, cutting off his wing and forcing a good save from Safonov shortly after coming on.
